pr.title: Have the CLI find a moved store in the app's iCloud container
pr.head: c1dad9c8675fc8d342a1d6c8b7bebea59f82cc7e

summary: multipass is a command-line password manager whose store is a package: a folder of encrypted files, by default ~/.multipass/store.multipass. The passkeys plan adds a Mac and iPhone app that keeps that package in the app's iCloud container, the app's own folder in iCloud Drive, so every device shares one store. On a Mac, the app moves an existing package out of ~/.multipass and into the container.

After that move, ~/.multipass holds no store. At the base, the CLI reached the container only through MULTIPASS_STORE, set from an export line the app shows. Without it, every command found no store, and multipass init would create a second, empty store that no other device sees.

This pull request changes only the plan. It decides, as § 6 question 10, that when neither --store nor MULTIPASS_STORE is set and ~/.multipass holds neither store.multipass nor store.age, the CLI's default becomes the container's package when it exists. init then finds that package and refuses, and the export line becomes optional. Two guards keep the CLI from saving where no other device reads:

• Both locations hold a store. A store can still appear in ~/.multipass later, such as from init on a second Mac before iCloud Drive lists the package. Every command then fails, naming both paths and the export line that picks each.
  • An explicit path names the old location. When --store or MULTIPASS_STORE names a path with no store while the container holds one, the error names the container. init still creates the store you named, after a note on stderr.

The user chose this answer, so question 10 is decided. It names the rejected alternative in one sentence: keep ~/.multipass as the only default, reach the container only through the export line, and have init only warn when the container holds a store. The plan stays a draft for question 5, which the prototype answers.

cards.title: Where the CLI looks for the store
cards.html:
1. --store, when passed.
  2. MULTIPASS_STORE, when set.
  3. ~/.multipass/store.multipass, or ~/.multipass/store.age, which the vault-key plan moves into a package.
  4. New: the container's Documents/store.multipass, when it exists.
  5. Otherwise ~/.multipass/store.multipass, where init creates one.

When steps 3 and 4 both find a store, every command fails and names both.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The review of ccefa45 found that a store appearing later in ~/.multipass silently took the CLI off the container, and made four suggestions. e1527c5 fixed the finding and took all four.
  • The review of e1527c5 was clean, with one suggestion: have the README.md row document the refusal when both locations hold a store. c1dad9c takes it, and its incremental review is clean.
  • The plan stays draft, so it makes no readiness claim.

groups.title: The CLI's fallback to the container
groups.kicker: Question 10 and the rows of the passkeys plan that follow from it
intro: Every edit is in the passkeys plan. Question 10 in § 6 states the problem and the decided answer, and the other edits make the rest of the plan agree with that answer.

• § 2.4's table says the CLI finds the container by itself, refuses to choose when both locations hold a store, and that the export line is then optional.
  • § 2.5's src/main.rs row gives the rule, the path ~/Library/Mobile Documents/<container>/Documents/store.multipass, how the folder is named, both guards, and the --store help line.
  • § 2.5's README.md row says the README documents the fallback, and the refusal when both locations hold a store, with the export line its error names.
  • § 4 expects init to refuse on the moved Mac, and adds a row for each guard.
  • § 8 step 1 adds a prototype check for a package iCloud Drive has not downloaded or has evicted.

checks.text: The container is the app's folder in iCloud Drive. On a Mac it sits under ~/Library/Mobile Documents/. A package there may be listed before its files have downloaded, which is what the new prototype check covers.

files.note: The passkeys plan: question 10 decides the CLI's fallback to the container and its two guards, and § 2.4, § 2.5, § 4 and § 8 follow it.

checks.text: § 4's expected error matches the one init gives today in run in src/main.rs, a store already exists at <path>, read at the head.
The folder under Mobile Documents is the container identifier with each . replaced by ~, as iCloud names every app's folder there.
The refusal runs before the vault-key plan's § 2.6 moves a local store.age into a package, so a stray old file never becomes a second local package.
